title: Fine internal networks and granules seen in fixed cells are largely artefacts

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fine internal networks and granules seen in fixed cells are largely artefacts

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Fixation preserves the general outward form of small organisms and cells, but the minute internal networks and granules described as the structure of protoplasm are to a large extent artefacts of coagulating fixatives, although larger structures such as nucleus, vacuoles, centrosomes and the spindle are really present in the living cell.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: While this assumption is reasonable and justified as regards the general outward form of small organisms or of individual cells, enough has been done of late years to shew that the case is totally different in the case of the minute internal networks, granules, etc., which represent the alleged _structure_ of protoplasm.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Fixation artefacts and living structure”. Scope: histological preparations of cells fixed with chemical reagents

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim makes a direct method-comparison prediction, and public correlative imaging can distinguish pre-existing structures from fixation products. Scope across all historical reagents is imperfect, but the central empirical generalization is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Register live-cell images with the same cells or matched samples after chemical fixation and quantify appearance, disappearance, and distortion of fine networks and granules versus larger organelles. A high fraction of fixation-specific fine structures alongside preservation of larger structures supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Modern fixation methods differ from those Thompson criticized.

Precisely matched live-to-fixed cells are less common than unmatched images.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim names which structures should survive a live-versus-fixed comparison and which should not. Public correlative imaging already contains that comparison for standard cell types and common fixatives, and the analysis is a classification of structures rather than a new method. Coverage is incomplete for the whole history of histological technique, but it is sufficient to confirm or refute the claim that the fine texture is largely artefactual.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score fine cytoplasmic networks and granules in chemically fixed cells against the same cells or matched living cells, and separately score nucleus, vacuoles, centrosomes and spindle. Fine texture present in fixed cells and absent in living cells, with the larger organelles retained, would support the claim; the same fine texture in living cells would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some granules are real and some are precipitates, so a single global fraction is an average over structures.

Not every historical fixative is represented by a correlative live-fixed pair.

analysis feasibility: 0.7

data existence: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.82
